editorial:
Imagine you are just trying to make a few extra bucks driving for a rideshare app late at night. That is exactly where you find Ayaan Malik, a regular guy who thinks he is just picking up one last passenger. But the person in the back seat is not your typical rider. They won't tell you where they are going, and suddenly, the city you know by heart starts acting weird. You will feel the tension grow as Ayaan realizes he is driving in circles on roads that should not exist. It feels like a bad dream that you cannot wake up from, and the vibe is super creepy and mysterious from the start.

What really makes this work is how the suspense builds slowly until it hits you all at once. The acting is great, and the twists will actually surprise you. While some parts of the middle feel a bit slow, the payoff is totally worth it. If you love movies that make you question what is real, you need to see this.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that Ayaan is actually in a loop caused by a car accident he had earlier that night. The mysterious passenger is actually a version of his own conscience or a guide. To escape the repeating roads, Ayaan has to admit his mistakes and let go of his guilt. Once he accepts the truth, the loop breaks, and he finally wakes up in the hospital, surviving the crash.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological twists and spooky urban settings.
